resources.string: Catch it before it flies off

A thought comes and goes in a second. Write it down here in two: from the widget, the tile in the quick settings, «Share» in any app, or by voice. No titles, no folders. It sticks to the web, and that’s it.

Press a thought and drag a thread to another. The more threads, the closer it moves to the middle: that’s how your real themes show. Every morning dew falls on a few old thoughts. Untied ones the wind takes away after a month.

When five thoughts or more hang together, spin them into a cocoon. In three days it ripens: reread what’s inside, sum it up in one sentence, and a butterfly flies out. The collection of butterflies is the thoughts that grew into something.
The web: %1$d thoughts. Tap one to open it, press and drag to tie it to another.
Catch the first thought: whatever is in your head right now.
Press a thought and drag a thread to another one
The cocoon «%1$s» is ripe. Open it
A thought, a question, something you noticed…
Write or say a thought in two seconds
A firefly: something to make, try or do.
A burr with a hook: it clings until you answer it. A question can be hung as a lure.
Dandelion down: something seen, heard, felt.
A wisp of someone else’s silk: a quote, a line, a phrase overheard.
Caught in the night. It will glow.
Almost the same as «%1$s». They hang side by side now, on a thicker thread.
Both thoughts are safe from the wind now.
They are in the Fluff, on the Thoughts tab. Nothing is lost.
It ripens in three days. No peeking.
This thought is inside a cocoon.
The wind took this thought to the Fluff.
Hung as a lure: in the evening, today’s catch is offered to it.
%1$d more thoughts in this cluster and it can be spun into a cocoon.
The thought goes to the Fluff, and its threads are cut. You can put it back from there.
It goes for good, with its threads.
These thoughts leave the web and ripen together for three days. Then you open the cocoon and say in one sentence what it all comes to.
Spin a cocoon from this cluster
Picked %1$d. A cocoon holds %2$d to %3$d thoughts.
Does anything caught today belong to this question? Tap to tie it.
Caught after midnight. Read it in daylight.
Nothing like that on the web.
What the wind took: thoughts that hung untied and untouched for %1$d days. They’re not lost. Put one back if it still matters.
The wind hasn’t taken anything yet.
No butterflies yet. Tie %1$d thoughts or more into one cluster, spin them into a cocoon, and three days later the first one flies out.
Thoughts ripen in the dark. When it’s ripe, you’ll reread them all at once and see what they add up to.
Read them all, slowly. What do they add up to? A decision, a plan, a first line, a «no»: one sentence.
«On Saturday I run the first tour for three friends.» «Not now, and that’s fine.»
The thoughts go back on the web with their threads. No butterfly.
September: gossamer flies. Pick the year’s twelve thoughts.
In September gossamer flies across the fields. Pick up to %1$d thoughts from the past year: the ones that stayed with you, came true, or changed something.
How long an untied thought nobody looked at hangs on the web before the wind takes it to the Fluff. Tying or rereading resets it.
Long-press the app icon for «Catch» and «Say it». Select text in any app or tap «Share» to catch it. And:
Put the widget on the home screen
Add a tile to quick settings
Everything lives only on this phone. Save a copy to move it or to read it anywhere.
Gossamer is made by one person. Bugs, ideas and news go through the StillCraft bot in Telegram.
A message when a new version is out
Talk to other people who use the apps
Gossamer %1$s. Free, no ads, no accounts, no internet. Fonts: Cormorant, Lora, Caveat (SIL OFL). MIT licence.
